## The Talent Risk of Return-to-Office Mandates

Return-to-office (RTO) mandates are a talent decision as well as an operations one. An earlier version of this article quoted turnover, application and acceptance figures, and attributed some to named research. We removed all of them because we could not source them to a specific study. The question is still worth asking: what would a mandate do to your own hiring and retention?

### What to Measure Instead

Use your own data to estimate the impact before and after any policy change:

- Voluntary turnover, by team, level and tenure
- Application volume and quality per open role
- Offer acceptance rate, defined as accepted offers divided by offers extended
- Time to fill for roles that require office presence
- Employee survey results on flexibility

### Who May Be Affected

Policies can affect groups differently. Look at turnover and offer acceptance by group in your own data, including parents and caregivers, senior employees, people with long commutes and people who live outside commuting distance. A policy that looks neutral can lose exactly the people you most want to keep. Do not assume the pattern, measure it.

### What Companies Can Do Instead

#### If You Need In-Person Collaboration

Design your policy around purpose, not presence:

- "Come in for workshops, planning and team-building"
- "Core collaboration days with flexibility otherwise"
- "Team-chosen schedules based on project needs"

#### If You Want Culture

Culture is built through intentional rituals, not proximity alone:

- Regular all-hands events
- Team offsites
- Virtual social activities
- Mentoring programs
- Cross-team projects

#### If You Want Accountability

Accountability comes from clear expectations, not surveillance:

- Output-based performance measures
- Regular 1:1 check-ins
- Project milestones and deadlines
- Transparent goal tracking

### Making the Case to Leadership

If leadership is considering an RTO mandate, present your own analysis:

- A turnover cost estimate using your own salary and replacement-cost inputs
- The recruiting impact you expect, based on your own application data
- A comparison of competitor policies, with sources
- Employee survey results
- Productivity data, if you have reliable measures
